author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Russia’s annual Victory Day celebration in Moscow looked dramatically different this year as President Vladimir Putin presided over a scaled-down military parade amid growing security concerns linked to the war in Ukraine.

No heavy military equipment rolled through Red Square, fireworks were cancelled, and public events across Victory Park were shut down due to fears of possible Ukrainian drone attacks. Instead, video displays showcased Russian military hardware currently being used on the Ukrainian frontlines.

During the ceremony, Putin compared Russia’s war in Ukraine to the Soviet Union’s fight during World War II and praised troops involved in the “special military operation.” North Korean troops reportedly involved in Russia’s Kursk operations also marched in the parade.

Meanwhile, Moscow and Kyiv agreed to a temporary 3-day ceasefire and prisoner exchange reportedly mediated by US President Donald Trump.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A massive cyberattack has hit Canvas, one of the world’s largest online learning platforms, disrupting schools and universities across multiple countries.

The hacking group “Shiny Hunters” claims to have stolen 3.5 terabytes of sensitive student data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and private messages. Around 275 million users may be affected.

The attack comes during exam season, forcing major universities like Harvard, Columbia, Penn State, and Georgetown to extend deadlines and reschedule exams as students lose access to coursework and assignments.

description:
The UK’s local elections have delivered a major political blow to Prime Minister Keir Starmer and the Labour Party.

Labour lost councils across England, including long-held strongholds, sparking calls from some MPs for Starmer to step down. Meanwhile, Nigel Farage’s Reform UK made major gains by campaigning heavily on immigration and attracting voters from both Labour and the Conservatives.

The results highlight a rapidly changing and increasingly fragmented political landscape in Britain ahead of future national elections.
